text: This map applies the coproduct to the coefficient of M⊗C, sending m⊗c to Σ(m⊗c₁)⊗c₂. Reassociation puts the resulting coefficient on the right. It realizes the cofree coaction of [Wisbauer, §1.14](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6) for the functor M↦M⊗C; M needs only its module structure, with no pre-existing coaction. Checks pass: [cofreeCoact_def](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L80), [cofree_coact_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L161).
The map is exactly id⊗Δ followed by inverse reassociation.
The selected cofree structure evaluates by the stated coproduct formula.

The coproduct equips M⊗C with its cofree right C-comodule structure. Coassociativity and the counit law come directly from those of C, implementing [Wisbauer, §1.14](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6). The construction explicitly selects this coaction because a tensor module may carry others; neither multiplication on C nor a coaction on M is required. Checks pass: [cofree_coact_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L161), [rTensor_rid_comp_lTensor_counit_comp_cofreeCoact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L178).
The packaged coaction has the expected value on elementary tensors.
The middle-factor counit gives the retraction used by the universal property.

The coaction of the selected cofree structure is id_M⊗Δ_C followed by reassociation into (M⊗C)⊗C. This identifies the actual structure implementing [Wisbauer, §1.14](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6). The equation concerns that particular coaction on M⊗C, rather than every possible comodule structure on the same carrier; tensor associativity changes parentheses, not factor order. Checks pass: [cofreeCoact_def](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L80), [cofree_coact_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L161).
The implementation unfolds to precisely the same linear composite.
The identified composite gives the coproduct formula on pure tensors.

On an elementary tensor m⊗c, the cofree coaction is Σ(m⊗c₁)⊗c₂, with Δ(c)=Σc₁⊗c₂. This is the tensor-comonad instance of [Wisbauer, §1.14](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6). The displayed inverse associator accounts for parentheses; the formula does not select a basis or require any particular presentation of the coproduct as a sum. Checks pass: [cofreeCoact_def](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L80), [rTensor_rid_comp_lTensor_counit_comp_cofreeCoact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L178).
The underlying map applies the coproduct to the right factor.
Applying the counit to c₁ recovers the original tensor.

After coacting on m⊗c, this composite applies ε to the middle coefficient c₁, giving Σm⊗ε(c₁)c₂=m⊗c. The tensor-unit map absorbs the scalar into M. This is the counit retraction used in [Wisbauer, §1.14](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6); specifying the actual factor avoids ambiguity about the names of the left and right counit laws. Checks pass: [cofree_coact_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L161), [cofreeLift_rid_comp_lTensor_counit_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L331).
The coaction exposes the two coefficient factors in their actual order.
The retraction recovers a comodule morphism from its counit component.

A linear map f:M→N induces f⊗id_C between the cofree comodules, leaving the coalgebra coefficient unchanged. Naturality of the coproduct proves compatibility with their coactions. This is the morphism operation of the cofree functor in [Wisbauer, §1.14](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6); neither M nor N needs a prior comodule structure. Checks pass: [cofreeMap_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L206), [cofreeMap_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L225).
The underlying map is exactly f⊗id_C.
The construction preserves composition of linear maps.

The coaction ρ_P itself is a comodule morphism P→P⊗C when the target carries the cofree coaction. Its compatibility is precisely coassociativity of ρ_P. This gives the unit of the forgetful–cofree adjunction in [Wisbauer, §1.14](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6); the word unit refers to that adjunction, not to a multiplicative identity in C. Checks pass: [cofreeUnit_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L246), [cofreeUnit_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L252).
The underlying linear map is the original coaction.
Evaluation retains the actual value ρ_P(p).

An ordinary linear map g:P→M from a C-comodule lifts to (g⊗id_C)ρ_P:P→M⊗C. Coassociativity makes this a comodule morphism into the cofree target, realizing the inverse correspondence in [Wisbauer, §1.14](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6). The map g need not preserve any coaction on M, because no such coaction is assumed. Checks pass: [cofreeLift_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L264), [rid_comp_lTensor_counit_comp_cofreeLift](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L325).
The lift has exactly the stated underlying composite.
Taking its counit component recovers the original map g.

The lifted comodule morphism has underlying linear map (g⊗id_C)ρ_P. Thus the construction adds a compatibility proof without changing that composite, as required by the cofree correspondence of [Wisbauer, §1.14](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6). The notation rTensor places g on the left carrier factor and leaves the right coalgebra coefficient unchanged. Checks pass: [cofreeLift_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L270), [rid_comp_lTensor_counit_comp_cofreeLift](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L325).
Evaluation agrees with applying g to the carrier factor of the coaction.
The counit projection returns g.

The cofree lift sends p to (g⊗id_C)(ρ_P(p)), or Σg(p₀)⊗p₁ in Sweedler notation. This concretely evaluates the inverse correspondence in [Wisbauer, §1.14](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6). The coaction value can be any tensor, including a sum of elementary tensors; neither a basis nor a finite-dimensionality assumption is needed. Checks pass: [cofreeLift_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L264), [cofreeEquiv_symm_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L319).
The full linear map is the same composite.
The inverse of the universal correspondence is precisely this lift.

Comodule morphisms P→M⊗C correspond bijectively to linear maps P→M: apply the counit to the coefficient to go forward, and send g to (g⊗id_C)ρ_P to go back. This is [Wisbauer, §1.14](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6), with the cofree functor right adjoint to forgetting the coaction. The proof requires neither flatness nor finite-dimensionality. Checks pass: [rid_comp_lTensor_counit_comp_cofreeLift](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L325), [cofreeLift_rid_comp_lTensor_counit_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L331).
Counit projection after lifting returns the linear map.
Lifting the counit component returns the comodule morphism.

The forward universal correspondence sends φ:P→M⊗C to its counit component πφ, where π(m⊗c)=ε(c)m. The right tensor-unit identification absorbs the scalar into M. This is the explicit forward map in [Wisbauer, §1.14](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6); φ is a comodule morphism, and the result is an ordinary linear map. Checks pass: [rid_comp_lTensor_counit_comp_cofreeLift](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L325), [cofreeLift_rid_comp_lTensor_counit_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L331).
This forward map undoes the cofree lift.
The same counit component determines φ uniquely.

The inverse universal correspondence sends an ordinary linear map g:P→M to the cofree lift (g⊗id_C)ρ_P. This is the inverse of the counit-component map in [Wisbauer, §1.14](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6). The inverse acts between spaces of morphisms; it does not assert that g, the coaction, or the counit projection is invertible. Checks pass: [cofreeLift_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L270), [rid_comp_lTensor_counit_comp_cofreeLift](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L325).
The inverse has the concrete value (g⊗id_C)(ρ_P(p)).
Taking the counit component recovers g.

Applying π(m⊗c)=ε(c)m after the cofree lift of g returns g. Indeed, the counit law for P reduces Σg(p₀)ε(p₁) to g(p). This is one inverse identity of [Wisbauer, §1.14](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6). The tensor-unit map performs scalar multiplication in M, rather than discarding the scalar coefficient. Checks pass: [cofreeLift_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L264), [cofreeEquiv_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L308).
The lift is the carrier-map tensor identity composed with the coaction.
The forward correspondence is exactly this counit projection.

A comodule morphism φ:P→M⊗C is recovered by lifting its counit component πφ. Colinearity of φ and the coalgebra counit law give this inverse identity of [Wisbauer, §1.14](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6). The comodule-morphism hypothesis is essential: the statement does not claim that an arbitrary linear map into M⊗C is determined by its counit component. Checks pass: [cofreeEquiv_symm_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L319), [rTensor_rid_comp_lTensor_counit_comp_cofreeCoact](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L178).
The inverse correspondence is the specified lift.
The middle-factor counit retraction supplies the recovery identity.

A comodule morphism into M⊗C vanishes exactly when its counit component vanishes. The bijection in [Wisbauer, §1.14](https://www.math.uni-duesseldorf.de/~wisbauer/Coalgebraic.pdf#page=6) is injective and sends the zero morphism to zero, giving both directions. This detects zero among comodule morphisms into the cofree target; it does not assert that the counit projection M⊗C→M is itself injective. Checks pass: [cofreeLift_rid_comp_lTensor_counit_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L331), [cofreeEquiv_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Cofree.lean#L308).
Every such morphism is reconstructed from its counit component.
The bijection uses exactly the stated counit projection.

Reassociation commutes with applying f:C→D to the two coefficient factors produced by a linear map ρ:M→M⊗C. Both sides give the same carrier and ordered coefficient factors. This supplies the bookkeeping for right corestriction in [Aguiar, Chapter 3, p.30](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~maguiar/thesis2.pdf#page=38); the identity needs no coassociativity or counit condition on ρ itself. Checks pass: [comul_lTensor_lTensor](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Corestrict.lean#L66), [corestrictCoact_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Corestrict.lean#L187).
The companion identity transports the coproduct through the coefficient map.
Actual corestricted coactions compose in the same coefficient direction.

Applying f to a coefficient and then taking its coproduct agrees with first taking the coproduct and applying f to both output coefficients. Tensoring with the identity on M preserves this coalgebra-morphism law. It is the coassociativity compatibility needed by [Aguiar, Chapter 3, p.30](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~maguiar/thesis2.pdf#page=38); no injectivity, surjectivity, or multiplication on the coalgebras is required. Checks pass: [assoc_rTensor_lTensor_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Corestrict.lean#L50), [corestrict_coact_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Corestrict.lean#L169).
Reassociation aligns the two coefficient factors in the coaction calculation.
The actual corestricted structure applies precisely id_M⊗f.

The counit is unchanged after applying a coalgebra morphism f:C→D to the coefficient factor. Both sides still take values in M⊗R; applying the tensor-unit identification gives the usual scalar evaluation in M. This transports the counit law for [Aguiar, Chapter 3, p.30](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~maguiar/thesis2.pdf#page=38), using ε_Df=ε_C rather than invertibility of f. Checks pass: [corestrict_coact_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Corestrict.lean#L169), [corestrictCoact_id](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Corestrict.lean#L177).
The selected corestriction acts on exactly the coefficient factor.
Identity corestriction retains the original coaction.

A C-comodule morphism remains compatible after both coactions are postcomposed with id⊗f for a coalgebra map f:C→D. The construction retains its underlying linear map, giving the morphism operation of [Aguiar, Chapter 3, p.30](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~maguiar/thesis2.pdf#page=38). This changes the coefficient coalgebra covariantly; it neither takes an inverse image of the carrier nor requires f to be invertible. Checks pass: [corestrictHom_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Corestrict.lean#L228), [corestrictHom_comp](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Corestrict.lean#L284).
The underlying linear map is unchanged.
Corestriction respects composition of comodule morphisms.

Corestriction sends the identity morphism of M to the identity for its new D-coaction, because it leaves the underlying map unchanged. This is the identity law for the functor in [Aguiar, Chapter 3, p.30](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~maguiar/thesis2.pdf#page=38). The source and target use the explicitly corestricted coaction; the statement does not identify C-comodule and D-comodule structures. Checks pass: [corestrictHom_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Corestrict.lean#L237), [corestrict_map_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Corestrict.lean#L332).
The transformed map has the same value on every vector.
The bundled functor retains the same underlying linear map.

Corestricting h∘g agrees with composing the corestricted morphisms, with g applied first. Both sides retain the same underlying composite, and coefficient postcomposition preserves their coaction compatibility. This is the composition law for [Aguiar, Chapter 3, p.30](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~maguiar/thesis2.pdf#page=38); the chosen D-coactions change the structures on the carriers without changing the maps between them. Checks pass: [corestrictHom_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Corestrict.lean#L228), [corestrict_map_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Corestrict.lean#L338).
Corestriction leaves the underlying maps unchanged.
The bundled functor evaluates a morphism by its original function.

A coalgebra map f:C→D gives a functor from right C-comodules to right D-comodules, replacing ρ by (id⊗f)ρ and retaining each underlying module and linear map. This is the right-handed corestriction explicitly included in [Aguiar, Chapter 3, p.30](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~maguiar/thesis2.pdf#page=38). Its direction follows f; unlike restriction of scalars for algebras, it is covariant in the coefficient map. Checks pass: [corestrict_obj](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Corestrict.lean#L323), [corestrict_map_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Corestrict.lean#L332).
Objects carry precisely the stated corestricted coaction.
Morphisms retain their original underlying linear maps.

A coalgebra map f:C→D is a D-comodule morphism from C with coaction (id_C⊗f)Δ_C to D with regular coaction Δ_D. Its compatibility is exactly Δ_Df=(f⊗f)Δ_C. This uses the corestriction of [Aguiar, Chapter 3, p.30](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~maguiar/thesis2.pdf#page=38); explicitly changing the source coaction is necessary because the two original regular comodules have different coefficient coalgebras. Checks pass: [toComoduleHom_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Corestrict.lean#L391), [toComoduleHom_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Corestrict.lean#L398).
The bundled morphism retains the original coalgebra map.
Its value at c is exactly f(c).

The regular-comodule morphism associated to f:C→D has underlying linear map f itself. The construction adds the coproduct-compatibility proof, after corestricting the regular source coaction to (id_C⊗f)Δ_C as in [Aguiar, Chapter 3, p.30](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~maguiar/thesis2.pdf#page=38). This defining equation identifies the actual map; it does not claim an equivalence of the source and target comodules. Checks pass: [toComoduleHom_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Corestrict.lean#L398), [corestrict_coact_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Corestrict.lean#L169).
Evaluation preserves the original value f(c).
The source coaction uses the stated coefficient postcomposition.

The complex field carries its usual Euclidean norm, |a+bi|=√(a²+b²), and distance |z−w|. The norm of a product is the product of the norms. This structure uses the existing complex arithmetic and metric; it does not choose an arbitrary equivalent norm. Compared with [Axler, 4.1–4.4](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Basic.lean#L65).

The complex numbers realize the real-or-complex interface with their usual real and imaginary parts, imaginary unit, conjugation and complete normed-field structure. Its auxiliary order compares real parts only when imaginary parts agree. Thus this is a partial order, not an ordering making all complex numbers comparable. Compared with [Axler, 4.1–4.4](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Basic.lean#L325).

Complex norm values meet every interval (r,s) with 0≤r<s: choose a positive real number between the endpoints and regard it as complex. “Densely normed” concerns the available norm values. It does not say that the real axis is dense in the complex plane. Compared with [Axler, 4.1–4.4](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Basic.lean#L69).

Every Cauchy sequence of complex numbers converges to a complex number. The source transfers completeness from the two real coordinates, using bounds in both directions between the complex Euclidean norm and the maximum norm on pairs. Completeness concerns limits of Cauchy sequences, not convergence of arbitrary bounded sequences. Compared with [Faris, §§17.1–17.2](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Basic.lean#L127).

Closed balls in the complex plane are compact. This is the familiar finite-dimensional Heine–Borel property: a closed bounded region fits inside a compact real coordinate box. The source transports this property through the coordinate correspondence and its metric bound. It does not assert that the whole complex plane is compact. Compared with [Faris, §§18.1–18.2](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Basic.lean#L141).

A complex seminormed vector space becomes a real seminormed vector space by allowing only real scalars, embedded in the complex field. The vectors, seminorm and topology stay the same. Lean permits a seminorm that vanishes on nonzero vectors here; neither positive definiteness nor completeness is added by restricting scalars. Compared with [Faris, §§16.2/23.3](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Basic.lean#L82).

The map r↦r+0i is packaged as a continuous real-linear map from the reals to the complex plane. It preserves the real norm and its image is the real axis. This inclusion goes from real to complex numbers; it is neither the real-part projection nor a surjection onto the plane. Compared with [Axler, §1A/4.2](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Basic.lean#L314).

Complex conjugation, a+bi↦a−bi, is a real-linear isometric bijection whose inverse is itself. It reflects the plane across the real axis and preserves distances. The scalar field matters: conjugation is real-linear, but multiplying an input by i shows that it is not complex-linear. Compared with [Axler, 4.1–4.4](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Basic.lean#L205).

Conjugation is also packaged as a continuous real-linear equivalence, with continuous inverse equal to conjugation. This is the same reflection a+bi↦a−bi used by the isometric version. Forgetting the explicitly recorded isometry changes the available structure, not the function or its inverse; complex linearity is not asserted. Compared with [Axler, 4.1–4.4](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Basic.lean#L252).

Conjugation is a continuous automorphism of the complex numbers as an algebra over the reals: it preserves addition, multiplication and one, fixes real scalars, and is its own inverse. The base field is essential. It is not an algebra automorphism over the complex numbers, since it sends i to −i. Compared with [Axler, 4.1–4.4](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Basic.lean#L247).

Taking the real part a+bi↦a is a continuous real-linear map, with |Re z|≤|z|. The estimate supplies continuity directly. The map loses the imaginary coordinate, so it is not injective; its real-linearity also should not be confused with preserving multiplication of arbitrary complex numbers. Compared with [Axler, 4.1–4.4](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Basic.lean#L152).

Taking the imaginary part a+bi↦b is a continuous real-linear map, with |Im z|≤|z|. Here the output is the real coefficient b, not the complex number bi. The map vanishes on the real axis and is not multiplicative; its scalar field is the reals. Compared with [Axler, 4.1–4.4](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Basic.lean#L172).

The coordinate map a+bi↦(a,b) is a continuous real-linear equivalence, with inverse (a,b)↦a+bi. Lean equips the pair with the maximum norm, rather than the Euclidean norm. Consequently this is not an isometry: 1+i has complex norm √2, while its coordinate pair has norm 1. Compared with [Faris, §16.3](https://math.arizona.edu/~faris/realweb/real.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Basic.lean#L134).

The real-axis inclusion r↦r+0i is a real-linear isometry into the complex plane: its norm remains |r| and distances between real inputs are unchanged. This construction records both linearity and norm preservation. It is an embedding into a larger space, not an equivalence onto every complex number. Compared with [Axler, §1A/4.2](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Basic.lean#L274).

Viewing real numbers as complex numbers preserves distances: the complex distance between x+0i and y+0i equals |x−y|. Thus the usual real line sits isometrically inside the complex plane. The coercion is exact for every real number, including negative and irrational values; no rounding or change of metric occurs. Compared with [Axler, §1A/4.2](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Basic.lean#L280).

Complex conjugation is continuous for the usual complex topology. Reflecting a+bi to a−bi leaves distances unchanged, so nearby inputs have equally nearby conjugates. This is ordinary continuity of a map of metric spaces; no choice of ordering on complex numbers or stronger notion of complex differentiability is involved. Compared with [Axler, 4.1–4.4](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Basic.lean#L237).

A real family sums to x exactly when its complex inclusion sums to x+0i, using the same summation filter. By default, sums are limits over all finite subsets, not merely ordered partial sums. Lean also allows the degenerate bottom filter, where every proposed sum satisfies the convergence relation. Compared with [Carneiro, df-tsms](https://us.metamath.org/mpeuni/df-tsms.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Basic.lean#L585).

If a complex family sums to z, its real parts sum to Re z along the same filter, because real part is continuous and additive. The hypothesis is actual convergence to z. Convergence of real parts alone does not imply convergence of the complex family; the imaginary parts may fail to converge. Compared with [Carneiro, df-tsms](https://us.metamath.org/mpeuni/df-tsms.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Basic.lean#L596).

A real family has a sum if and only if the same family, included in the complex numbers, has a sum along the same filter. Continuous inclusion and the real-part projection give the two directions. “Summable” means existence of a limit here; it is distinct from Lean assigning a default totalized sum. Compared with [Carneiro, df-tsms](https://us.metamath.org/mpeuni/df-tsms.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Basic.lean#L589).

Casting a real totalized sum into the complex numbers commutes with summation, without a convergence assumption. Lean assigns zero when no sum exists. The theorem also permits the bottom filter: every convergence assertion then holds, while the chosen total is the finite-support sum, or zero for infinite support. Casting preserves these conventions. Compared with [Carneiro, df-tsms](https://us.metamath.org/mpeuni/df-tsms.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Basic.lean#L593).

For a positive finite real matrix and positive margins, the plans obtained by repeated column-then-row normalization converge entrywise to any given positive scaling with those margins. The starting row factors may be any positive vector. Positivity makes the normalization denominators nonzero. The conclusion concerns the scaled matrices; it does not choose a normalization of their factors. See [Peyré–Cuturi, Theorem 4.2 and equation 4.23, pp.78–79](https://optimaltransport.github.io/pdf/ComputationalOT.pdf). Checks pass: [exact 2×2 family](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Data/Matrix/Scaling/Basic.lean#L327), [finite IPFP identification](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Finite/ProportionalFitting.lean#L135), [row sums](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Data/Matrix/Sinkhorn/Basic.lean#L337), [residual bounds](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Data/Matrix/Sinkhorn/Rate.lean#L262) and [objective-gap bounds](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Data/Matrix/Sinkhorn/Rate.lean#L280).
The existing computed family supplies the exact rational 2×2 scaling used to calibrate the finite algorithm.
The actual plan after each sweep has exactly the prescribed row sums.
Actual finite Radon–Nikodym IPFP agrees with matrix Sinkhorn, with the proved transpose and n+1 index convention.
The actual iterates have certified ℓ¹ column-residual bound(exp(t^(2n)Δ)−1)A.
The optimum primal value minus the current logarithmic-factor dual value is at most A t^(2n)Δ.

Every finite rectangular real matrix with positive entries can be multiplied by positive row and column factors to attain any positive prescribed margins of equal total mass. The displayed finite sums are exactly those margins; probability normalization is unnecessary. The existing product-coupling formula computes the required all-ones 2×2 case, with every scaled entry 1/2. See [Peyré–Cuturi, Proposition 4.3 and equations 4.12–4.13, pp.69–70](https://optimaltransport.github.io/pdf/ComputationalOT.pdf). Check passes: [the computed product family](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Data/Matrix/Scaling/Basic.lean#L327).
The explicit product family computes both margins, including the exact all-ones 2×2 scaling with entries 1/2.

A nonnegative finite real matrix admits positive diagonal factors with prescribed margins exactly when a nonnegative matrix with those margins has the same zero entries. Thus every allowed edge must remain positive. Nonnegative margins and equal total mass follow automatically; zero rows and columns correctly force zero target margins. See [Menon, Theorem 2 and the block-decomposition remark, pp.228,232](https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/E15F012AA4869A056F6EAB8E1AECB177/S0008414X00051592a.pdf/matrix-links-an-extremization-problem-and-the-reduction-of-a-non-negative-matrix-to-one-with-prescribed-row-and-column-sums.pdf). Checks pass: [exact 2×2 product family](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Data/Matrix/Scaling/Basic.lean#L327) and [positive scaling on the exact support](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Data/Matrix/Scaling/Basic.lean#L835).
The explicit family supplies the requested exact 2×2 row/column calibration.
A full-support feasible matrix makes the support-constrained entropy minimizer an actual scaling by strictly positive factors.
